raw_case_text:
A 40-year-old lady presented with fever, headache, arthralgia, and myalgia, after returning from the Philippines. She recalled mosquito bite one week before. Investigations showed lymphopenia, increased hepatic enzymes, C-Reactive-Protein (CRP), normal renal function (Table 1), and prominent spleen (11.6 cm) on ultrasonogram. Empirical antibiotic was given. Septic workup was negative. Her fever subsided and hepatic enzymes were improving. Dengue-virus IgM/specific nonstructural (NS1) protein antigen, chikungunya virus (CHIKV) IgM, and blood malaria parasite were not detected. She was discharged on day 10 with stable condition.
Eight weeks later she was readmitted for fever, malaise, and persistent symmetrical polyarthritis involving both wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, shoulders, hips, and knees, mimicking RA. She reported no recent hiking, no rash, and no oral ulcer. Clinical examination revealed more than ten tender and swollen joints over hands, wrists, and knees. There was no lymphadenopathy and no focal neurological deficit. Blood tests showed elevated liver enzymes, ferritin, and persistent high CRP level (Table 1). Hepatitis A, B, and C serology, anti-HIV, autoantibodies including rheumatoid factor, anticyclic-citrullinated peptide, anti-nuclear antibody, antidouble-stranded-DNA, anti-neutrophil-cytoplasmic antibody, anti-smooth-muscle antibody, and anti-mitochondrial antibody were all negative. C3 and C4 levels were normal. There was no erosion on hands and knees radiographs and her chest X-ray was clear. She was covered with Augmentin and Doxycycline for fever. No vegetation was detected on echocardiogram. Hepatic ultrasonogram showed prominent periportal echogenicity. Musculoskeletal ultrasound demonstrated wrists extensors and flexors tenosynovitis with increased Doppler signals, effusion, and synovial proliferation in knees (Figure 1). A total 25 mL fluid was aspirated from left knee suprapatellar recess. Gram stain, bacterial culture, and acid-fast-bacilli smear were negative. Fever persisted for two weeks. Liver biopsy was suggested to look for infective or infiltrative causes but patient refused. Septic workup was all unrevealing. CHIKV serology was rechecked. This time CHIKV-IgM was detected and CHIKV-polyvalent-antibody titre had risen from 1 : <10 to 1 : 1280. The first CHIKV-IgM negative sample was reexamined and was CHIKV-PCR positive (Table 1). The diagnosis of CHIKV-related arthritis was made. She was treated with supportive measures. Liver enzymes slowly reduced but joint symptoms persisted. Patient requested discharge-against-medical-advice after 3 weeks of hospital stay.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 40-year-old woman presented with fever, headache, arthralgia, and myalgia 1 week after a mosquito bite in the Philippines, followed 8 weeks later by readmission for persistent fever, malaise, and symmetrical rheumatoid-like polyarthritis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially presented after returning from the Philippines with acute fever, headache, arthralgia, and myalgia, improving over a 10-day hospitalization. Eight weeks later, she was readmitted with 2 weeks of persistent fever, malaise, and symmetric polyarthritis involving both wrists, MCP joints, shoulders, hips, and knees.
subjective.past_medical_history: Travel to the Philippines with a recalled mosquito bite 1 week prior to initial illness; no recent hiking on second admission.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for biphasic fever, headache, myalgia, malaise, and symmetrical polyarthritis (wrists, MCPs, shoulders, hips, knees). Negative for rash or oral ulcers.

objective.physical_examination: Second admission: >10 tender and swollen joints across bilateral hands, wrists, and knees; no lymphadenopathy, rash, oral ulcers, or focal neurological deficits.
objective.routine_investigations: First admission: lymphopenia, elevated hepatic enzymes and CRP, normal renal function, negative malaria smear, negative dengue IgM/NS1, negative initial CHIKV IgM, and 11.6 cm spleen on ultrasound. Second admission (8 weeks later): persistently elevated liver enzymes, ferritin, and CRP; negative HAV/HBV/HCV, HIV, RF, anti-CCP, ANA, anti-dsDNA, ANCA, ASMA, AMA, and normal C3/C4; normal hand/knee radiographs, CXR, and echocardiogram; hepatic ultrasound showing prominent periportal echogenicity; musculoskeletal ultrasound showing wrist flexor/extensor tenosynovitis with hyperemia and bilateral knee effusions/synovial proliferation; and sterile left knee arthrocentesis (25 mL; negative Gram stain, bacterial culture, and AFB smear).
objective.advanced_workup: Liver biopsy was recommended for persistent transaminitis and fever, but the patient declined.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV)-related chronic symmetrical polyarthritis and hepatitis, confirmed by CHIKV IgM seroconversion and a rise in CHIKV polyvalent antibody titer from <1:10 to 1:1,280 on the second admission, plus retrospective positive CHIKV RT-PCR on the initial acute-phase serum sample. Dengue was ruled out by negative dengue NS1 antigen and IgM testing. Managed with empiric amoxicillin-clavulanate/doxycycline and supportive care before the patient took discharge against medical advice at 3 weeks with improving liver enzymes and persistent arthralgia.
